newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Boeing says 777 cargo smoke alarms fix found.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says 777 cargo smoke alarms fix found.

text.p: Boeing Co. said it has developed a cure for cargo smoke detection systems in new Boeing 777 airliners which have been giving false alarms.

The manufacturer said in a statement received here that the "fix" will be certified by America's Federal Aviation Administration(FAA) in mid-October and a service bulletin issued to airlines before a retrofit programme is begun.

More than a dozen passengers were injured in June when more than 300 had to make an emergency evacuation from a Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd 777 which had just landed in Hong Kong. The false fire alarm is thought to have been caused by its belly cargo which included live frogs -- a popular Chinese food.
An Emirates 777 had a similar false alarm involving a cargo of mangoes. Both airlines imposed a ban on live or perishable cargo in their aircraft until a solution was found.
Boeing said until the problem was solved it had issued recommendations about cargoes with a high moisture content to other 777 operators.

Cargo smoke detection systems which use photoelectric sensors to 'look' for light reflected off air particles have a history of problems with dust and moisture which have caused false alarms in the past, it said.

Boeing said it was difficult during flight testing to replicate the exact environment the aircraft encounters in service -- such as dealing with live frogs and perishables with a high moisture content.
In-service problems which often took 12 to 16 months to fix had in this case been cured in 4-1/2 months, it added.
